title: North Korea fires intermediate-range missile, claiming evasive flight and AI features
key_facts: North Korea said on Saturday 4 Oct 2026 it test-fired an intermediate-range ballistic missile from the Wonsan area, overseen by Kim Jong Un.
Kim Yo Jong said the missile can change trajectory at low altitude and has unspecified AI capabilities that make it very hard to intercept; she called it 'strategic', implying a nuclear role.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it flew more than 700 km; Japan's Defense Ministry put it at about 680 km and said it landed outside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
Kim Yo Jong cited the gap between the allies' figures as proof they could not track it; South Korea often says the North exaggerates its capabilities.
The launch follows the 21 Sep 2026 landmine blasts that wounded three South Korean soldiers, which a UN Command inspection attributed to the North.
US Pacific Command said the launch 'does not pose an immediate threat' to US personnel, territory or allies.
quote_evidence: She also claimed it can alter its trajectory at low altitudes and has unspecified artificial intelligence capabilities, which she said would make it extremely hard to intercept.

Japan’s military said the missile landed in waters outside its exclusive economic zone, while the South Korean military, which often accuses North Korea of exaggerating its military capabilities, said the missile travelled more than 700 kilometres.
why_it_matters_hint: The launch is confirmed by South Korea and Japan; the AI claim is North Korea's alone and unverified.
notes: Launch confirmed by Seoul and Tokyo; the AI and evasive-flight features are Pyongyang's claims only.
